name: Epsilon Indi B
blurb: A pair of brown dwarfs orbiting the star Epsilon Indi, 12 light-years away. Brown dwarfs are too small to shine like stars but glow in the infrared.
astrometry_note: Linear proper motion from SIMBAD (epoch J2000); parallax ignored.
processing: SPHEREx Level-2 cutouts from IRSA (spherex_qr2, spherex_qr3). Flagged pixels (TRANSIENT, OVERFLOW, SUR_ERROR, PHANTOM, NONFUNC, MISSING_DATA, HOT, COLD, NONLINEAR, PERSIST, OUTLIER) masked; ZODI model and median background subtracted; bilinear reprojection to a 256×256 TAN grid; mean stack of up to 3 images per observing period and detector (wavelength varies between images — see each frame's range); shared asinh stretch per detector. Small masked holes are filled for display only (see flags overlay); saturated star cores are filled with the image maximum.
